otherFees: Application fee: UNVERIFIED (payable by credit card per the payments page, amount not published). Regional tax: included in the non-EU tuition figure. Graduation thesis fee: charged separately and explicitly EXCLUDED from scholarship coverage — amount UNVERIFIED. Materials/equipment fees: UNVERIFIED.

The International Postgraduate Scholarship competition awards partial first-year tuition of €2,200–€6,000 depending on programme and category; 'Non-EU (residence outside EU)' applicants to Master of Arts programmes receive UP TO €6,000. First academic year only; regional tax and thesis fee excluded. Deadline for the Oct-2026 intake was 27 May 2026; a further European postgraduate competition closed 24 July 2026. Two-year total: roughly €38,500–€44,500 in tuition alone.
reputationSignals: MUR/AFAM-recognised; internationally marketed with a large non-EU cohort; part of Galileo Global Education. Course leadership/area leadership named for the sister programme (Vincenzo Cuccia, a former SAE Institute coordinator, is Media Design area leader). Red flags: the non-EU price is roughly triple the EU-banded floor and there is no income banding for non-EU students; no equipment or studio inventory is published for a course that claims sound design as a strand; several key fees (application, thesis) are simply not disclosed.
acceptsNonMusic: Yes, in practice the most open door in this list. Entry needs 'Bachelor's degree/academic diploma' with no subject restriction, no audition, no music prerequisite — only a portfolio, a motivation letter and IELTS 5.0. A BSc in Software Engineering is a normal profile for a creative-technology MA.
recommendation: ACADEMICALLY REACHABLE, FINANCIALLY BRUTAL, AND NOT REALLY MUSIC PRODUCTION. This is the easiest official Italian second-cycle degree for him to be admitted to — no audition, no music degree, IELTS 5.0. But at €22,250/year for a non-EU student it costs nearly three times Saint Louis for a course that is about performance and interaction design with sound as one component, not about producing records or DJing. If he applies, apply through the scholarship competition (up to €6,000, portfolio-assessed) and treat the award as decisive: without it, the two-year €44,500 bill is not defensible for someone whose stated goal is club/electronic production.

Of everything in Italy this is the programme that most values his software-engineering background — the year-two creative-coding specialisation is essentially built for him. But it is audiovisual and interactive media, not music production, mixing or DJing; he would come out a creative technologist, not a producer. At €44,500 for two years that is an expensive way to end up in the wrong profession. Consider only if his ambition broadens toward audiovisual/interactive art.

recommendation: CHEAPER THAN NABA, BUT NOT A SOUND COURSE AND ITALIAN-ONLY. RUFA is a legitimate MUR-recognised private academy at roughly a third to a half of NABA's non-EU price, and the €100 application fee and 10% early bird are honest, published savings. But there is no sound design or music production master here, and the one course closest to his skills is taught exclusively in Italian with mandatory in-person attendance. Only worth pursuing if he commits to learning Italian to working level and reframes his goal toward multimedia/creative-AI design. For audio specifically, his own Saint Louis partnership is the better door.

It is genuinely about the music he wants to make, it is cheap by comparison at €6,400, and it is taught in real studios. But it is not a master, not a degree, gives no MUR title, is taught in Italian, and almost certainly will not carry a student visa. It is a course for someone already living in Milan. For a Tunisian national needing a visa in September 2027, it fails the threshold test.

program: Electronic Music Production (SAE Certificate)
institution: SAE Institute Milano

englishTest: IELTS not accepted or relevant — the requirement is ITALIAN at B2 CEFR.

tuitionTotal: UNVERIFIED.
otherFees: UNVERIFIED.

reputationSignals: Genuinely good course design for a producer — no exams, entirely project-driven, and it ends with a finished, mastered, release-ready EP including a remix. That output is precisely what a portfolio-less applicant needs. The Ableton and Pioneer DJ partnerships are real. The red flags are the unpublished price and the fact that it sits outside the AFAM recognition that makes SAE Milano credible.
totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED — no published figure. Milan living costs are the highest in Italy and are not offset by any scholarship access on this course.
recommendation: Right content, wrong language, wrong status. The syllabus is arguably the best-designed short electronic-production course found in this research — no exams, pure project work, ending in a mastered EP with an original remix, which is exactly the deliverable his empty portfolio needs. But it is taught in Italian with a certified B2 requirement, it carries no academic recognition of any kind, the price is unpublished, and it cannot be relied on for a visa. Rule out for September 2027. Note the structural lesson for him though: an 8-month project-based course whose output is a finished EP is a better portfolio-building instrument than a year of lectures — that is a criterion he should apply when choosing between any of these.

SAE Milan is probably the most genuinely hands-on audio training in this whole list, and its Yamaha and BASE Milano relationships are real. But its top Italian award is a bachelor-level diploma he already out-ranks, it offers nothing at master level, and it demands certified Italian at B2 from international students — a year of language study before he could even apply. If he wants SAE specifically he should look at SAE campuses in countries where the delivery is in English, not Milan.

program: Produzione Audio / Audio Production and Music Technologies — Diploma Accademico di Primo Livello
institution: SAE Institute Milano (SAE Italia S.R.L. International Technology College — SAE / Navitas global chain)
qualification: Diploma Accademico di PRIMO livello — a first-level (bachelor-equivalent) AFAM academic diploma, legally recognised by the Italian Ministry of University and Research. This is a genuine, official Italian qualification — but it is BACHELOR level, not a master. SAE Milano is authorised for first-level diplomas only; it is NOT authorised to award a Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello.
institutionType: International chain campus – specialist audio academy operating as a legally recognised non-state AFAM institute in Italy
focus: Audio production and music technologies: acoustics, recording, mixing, mastering, sound for film, live sound, game audio, immersive/spatial audio, AI in music production
whatYouStudy: Three years, 180 CFA credits. Core areas per the official course page: acoustics, recording, mixing, mastering, sound for film, live performance, game audio and immersive spaces. Lab-based, project-driven, with explicit coverage of AI in music production and spatial audio systems. Career outcomes listed: recording engineer, music producer, sound designer, live sound engineer, audio programmer for games.
durationEcts: 3 years, 180 CFA (the AFAM credit unit, equivalent in weight to ECTS).
language: Italian. International applicants must hold certified Italian language proficiency at minimum B2 CEFR. This is a hard barrier.

SAE Italia is a non-state institution operating inside the national AFAM framework, ministerially authorised to award official first-level academic diplomas under Ministerial Decree 280/2017 pursuant to Art. 11 of DPR 212/2005. program: MARKET-LEVEL FINDING — no private NVAO-accredited master in sound design or music production exists in the Netherlands
institution: Netherlands private higher-education sector (systematic check across NVAO/CROHO-registered private institutions and all named specialist audio providers)
qualification: NONE EXISTS. After searching in both English and Dutch ('master muziekproductie', 'opleiding sound design particulier', 'niet-bekostigde opleiding', 'master sound design Nederland particuliere hogeschool NVAO'), I found NO privately-run, NVAO-accredited master's degree in sound design, music production, audio engineering, music technology, immersive audio or electronic music performance anywhere in the Netherlands.
accreditationStatus: DEFINITIVE STRUCTURAL FINDING. In the Netherlands the audio/music education market splits cleanly in two, with nothing in between. (1) ACCREDITED = PUBLIC. Every NVAO-accredited master in this field belongs to a government-funded ('bekostigd') public institution: HKU Utrecht (Master of Music pathway Music Design; Sound Design and Audio Design at bachelor level), Conservatorium van Amsterdam / AHK (Master Immersive Audio — NVAO-assessed; plus the AEMA associate degree for electronic musicians, English-taught), Codarts Rotterdam, and the Institute of Sonology at the Royal Conservatoire in The Hague. These are all excluded from this brief as public. (2) PRIVATE = UNACCREDITED. Every private audio provider in the country (SAE, Abbey Road Institute, Sound Education, Pro Audio Education, DDMA, Master The Mix, AV Sound Education, DJ School Amsterdam, Music Production Academy) holds at most CRKBO and/or NRTO registration. CRKBO is a short-vocational-education register that governs VAT exemption; NRTO is a private-training trade association quality mark. NEITHER IS AN ACCREDITATION AND NEITHER CONFERS DEGREE STATUS. The sole exception — SAE's MA/MSc — is a UK University of Hertfordshire award delivered fully online, with no Dutch status and no campus component. Meanwhile private institutions that DO hold NVAO accreditation (Tio, Wittenborg, Nyenrode) operate exclusively in business and hospitality.

visaEligible: THE DECISIVE FINDING FOR THIS CANDIDATE — NO. Only an IND recognised sponsor can apply for a Dutch student residence permit on a student's behalf, and the IND study register covers higher professional/university education, senior secondary vocational education (ROCs) and IB schools. NOT ONE private specialist audio provider in the Netherlands is a recognised sponsor. Both of the two credible English-language schools say so themselves, in writing: SAE Institute Netherlands states 'SAE is a private Institute, its students are not eligible for a Visa, nor a student loan via DUO' and 'The registration at SAE Institute cannot grant you a Student Visa in the Netherlands'; Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam states 'Currently, we are not able to assist non-EU residents with their visa application to study in the Netherlands' and 'Since Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam is a private Institute, students are not eligible for a VISA or a student loan', adding that applicants may only attend if they already have 'a personal means of obtaining a VISA, for example, a family connection or registration at a university'. CONCLUSION: a Tunisian national CANNOT legally relocate to the Netherlands to study at any private audio school. Verify current status yourself at https://ind.nl/en/public-register-recognised-sponsors/public-register-study (updated monthly).
reputationSignals: The Dutch private audio market is small, expensive and structurally unable to serve non-EU students. The two brands worth respecting on teaching quality — SAE Institute Amsterdam and Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam — both disclose their inability to sponsor visas only in fine print (an entry-requirements sub-page and an FAQ respectively) while running international-facing marketing. That is the sector's central red flag. A second recurring red flag is nomenclature: Pro Audio Education titles its diploma 'Master Geluidstechniek' for what it concedes is MBO+/HBO- level work, and 'Master The Mix Academy' will surface in any search for a music-production master. Neither is a master's degree. A third is opacity: three providers (Master The Mix, AV Sound Education, Music Production Academy) publish no prices at all.
recommendation: BOTTOM LINE FOR THE NETHERLANDS: DO NOT BUILD THE SEPTEMBER 2027 PLAN AROUND A DUTCH PRIVATE SCHOOL. There is no private NVAO-accredited master in this field in the country, and no private audio provider can sponsor his residence permit — so the two things he needs (an accredited master + a visa) are simply not purchasable from the Dutch private sector at any price. He should concentrate his accredited-master applications on the Spain/Portugal/Italy slices, or reconsider Dutch PUBLIC institutions, which are outside this brief but are the only Dutch route that actually works: the Conservatorium van Amsterdam's Master Immersive Audio (NVAO-assessed) and its English-taught AEMA associate degree for electronic musicians — where, notably, 'when you enroll in an Associate Degree course, you can apply for a visa' — and HKU's Master of Music pathway Music Design. TWO THINGS HE CAN USEFULLY DO IN THE NETHERLANDS ANYWAY, both on an ordinary Schengen tourist visa and neither requiring accreditation: (1) DJ School Amsterdam's Producer Professional Course, ~€2,499 for 20 one-to-one English-language sessions plus 10 studio hours, compressible into two weeks — a direct, efficient way to build the portfolio he lacks; (2) SAE Amsterdam's one-month DJ Certificate at €699–€1,099 (confirm whether the €500 registration fee applies), ideally timed around Amsterdam Dance Event in October for scene contacts. Both are training, not qualifications — but a 4–8 track portfolio built to Abbey Road's published standard is precisely what every accredited master he applies to will ask for, and he does not have one yet. That is the highest-value use of the Netherlands for him.

program: MA/MSc Professional Practice in Creative Media Industries — Audio Production specialism
institution: SAE Institute Amsterdam (SAE Institute Netherlands, part of the global SAE / Navitas chain)
city: Amsterdam (delivered fully ONLINE — no campus attendance)
qualification: UK Master's degree (MA or MSc) awarded by the University of Hertfordshire. NOT a Dutch degree, NOT NVAO-accredited. This is the only thing at a private Dutch audio institution that is genuinely a master.
accreditationStatus: NOT NVAO. The award is a UK degree 'developed, delivered and assessed by SAE Institute, and awarded by and quality assured by the University of Hertfordshire' (site footer, 2025/6 programmes). SAE Institute Netherlands itself is only registered with CRKBO (Centraal Register Kort Beroepsonderwijs = short vocational education register) — CRKBO is a VAT/quality register for short vocational training, it is NOT a degree accreditation and confers no Dutch higher-education status. In practice: a UK-recognised master's degree, valid in the EHEA via the UK award, but with zero Dutch legal status. Institution is 'niet-bekostigd' (private, unfunded).
institutionType: International chain campus — specialist audio/creative-media academy (SAE operates ~50 campuses worldwide)
focus: Self-directed, project-based professional practice master. Student develops one major creative project in a chosen specialism; Audio Production is one of the available specialisms (others: Music Business, Film, Game Art, Games Programming, VFX, Web Dev, Content Creation).
durationEcts: 1 year full-time or 2 years part-time. ECTS value UNVERIFIED (UK master's, normally 180 UK credits = 90 ECTS).
entryRequirements: Three routes: (1) Bachelor degree with Honours at 2:2 or higher in a RELEVANT field PLUS 1 year work experience; (2) at least five years of professional creative-industry experience; (3) completion of SAE's PGCert Professional Development. SAE states the programme accepts applicants without a media-specific degree.
acceptsNonMusic: PARTIALLY — SAE states applicants without a media-specific degree are accepted, but the published route reads 'Bachelor degree with Honours (2:2 or higher) in a relevant field, plus 1 year's work experience'. A BSc Software Engineering could plausibly be argued as relevant for games/audio programming, but the candidate has NO professional audio experience and NO work experience, so he fails the '+1 year work experience' element and the 5-year-experience route. Route 3 (SAE's own PGCert Professional Development) is the realistic entry — that is an extra paid course. Confirm directly with SAE.
englishTest: IELTS accepted. Postgraduate: IELTS 6.5 overall with minimum 5.5 in each band. Alternatives listed: TOEFL 79, Cambridge C1 Advanced 176 / C2 180, Duolingo 120, PTE, LanguageCert. He has NOT taken IELTS — this must be booked well before applying.
portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED on the published pages. The programme is project-based, so a project proposal is likely required; confirm with admissions.
auditionSpec: None published (UNVERIFIED — likely an admissions interview given the self-directed format).
whatYouStudy: No fixed taught curriculum. Student negotiates a personal learning contract and produces a major self-directed creative/professional project in Audio Production, supported by weekly webinars, supervisor meetings and virtual conferences. This is a reflective/professional-practice master, NOT a hands-on studio craft course.
facilities: NONE — the programme is fully online. No studio access, no console time, no Atmos room, no live-electronics lab. SAE Amsterdam's physical facilities (Audient consoles, Pro Tools, Ableton rigs, recording studios) belong to the on-campus diploma/degree programmes, not this master.
equipmentRequired: Own computer and DAW required (implied by online delivery). Exact spec/licence list UNVERIFIED for the master. For SAE's on-campus courses the site says a personal laptop is 'recommended but not required' because campus workstations are provided — that does not apply to an online master.

totalCostEstimate: Approximately £6,750 (~€7,900 at typical rates) tuition for the whole programme, plus possible €500 registration, plus his own computer/DAW/licences and IELTS fee. This is by far the cheapest 'master' in this slice — because it is online and delivers no studio time. Living costs are NOT incurred since there is no relocation.
visaEligible: NO. Two independent reasons: (1) the programme is fully online, so there is nothing to relocate for; (2) SAE Institute Netherlands states in writing on its entry-requirements page: 'SAE is a private Institute, its students are not eligible for a Visa, nor a student loan via DUO', and on its course pages: 'The registration at SAE Institute cannot grant you a Student Visa in the Netherlands.' Only an IND-recognised sponsor can apply for a Dutch student residence permit, and SAE Amsterdam does not do this.
reputationSignals: POSITIVE: SAE is the largest audio-education chain in the world (founded 1976, ~50 campuses), the Amsterdam campus has real professional studios with Audient consoles and Pro Tools/Ableton, and degrees are quality-assured by a real UK university (University of Hertfordshire; Middlesex University for pre-2022 enrolments). RED FLAGS: (a) the awarding partner changed from Middlesex to Hertfordshire in 2022 — validation partnerships at SAE are not permanent; (b) the 'master' has no studio component whatsoever despite being marketed by a studio school; (c) SAE Amsterdam's inability to sponsor a visa is disclosed only in the small print of the entry-requirements page; (d) prices for on-campus programmes are very high relative to Dutch public alternatives (Quora threads flag exactly this). Notable alumni/staff for the Amsterdam campus: UNVERIFIED — the site publishes testimonials rather than named industry staff. Graduate employment outcomes: UNVERIFIED (no published stats).
recommendation: DO NOT ENROL for his stated goal. He wants to become an international DJ/producer and wants hands-on craft — this master delivers zero studio hours, zero console time, zero live electronics, and no relocation to a scene. It is a reflective professional-practice wrapper designed for people who ALREADY have a creative career. He has none, and on paper he does not even meet the entry route (bachelor in a relevant field PLUS one year's work experience). It also cannot support a Dutch residence permit, so it does not get him to Amsterdam. The only scenario where it makes sense is years from now, once he already works in audio and wants a formal master's title cheaply. Skip for September 2027.

qualification: BA/BSc (Hons) — a UK BACHELOR degree awarded and quality-assured by the University of Hertfordshire. This is a real degree, but it is an undergraduate one and a UK one, delivered in the Netherlands. NOT a master. He already holds a BSc, so this would be a sideways step.
institutionType: International chain campus – specialist audio academy (SAE / Navitas), UK-validated
focus: Audio engineering and music production to bachelor level
whatYouStudy: Recording, mixing, mastering, sound design, studio practice and audio engineering across the full degree. Detailed module list UNVERIFIED.
durationEcts: 24 months (Fast Track) or 36 months (Standard). UK credit structure; ECTS equivalence UNVERIFIED.
accreditationStatus: Not Dutch-accredited. NO NVAO accreditation — SAE Amsterdam is niet-bekostigd and holds only CRKBO short-vocational registration in the Netherlands. The degree's standing comes entirely from the UK: 'developed, delivered and assessed by SAE Institute, and awarded by and quality assured by the University of Hertfordshire.' (Students enrolled before 1 January 2022 were under Middlesex University.) So the award is a recognised UK bachelor's degree, but the Dutch delivery site has no Dutch higher-education status.
visaEligible: NO. Despite being a genuine degree, SAE Netherlands states that 'SAE is a private Institute, its students are not eligible for a Visa' and 'The registration at SAE Institute cannot grant you a Student Visa in the Netherlands.' Non-EU students must already hold a valid visa covering the entire course before enrolling. This is the crucial trap: the degree is real, the residence permit is not available.
acceptsNonMusic: Yes — SAE weighs creative potential over academic history; his BSc more than satisfies entry. But entering a bachelor's with a bachelor's already in hand is the wrong move.
entryRequirements: Age 18+, intermediate level of education, English proficiency (see below), laptop recommended.
englishTest: IELTS accepted and required for degree courses: IELTS 6.0 for undergraduate entry with minimum 5.5 in each band. Alternatives: TOEFL 72, Duolingo 120, Cambridge B2 First/C1/C2, GCSE/IGCSE English grade C or above. Note IELTS 6.0 is a far softer target than Berklee's 7.5.
intakes: Two per year: March and September.
deadline: No published deadline — rolling admissions. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
tuitionPerYear: 2026/2027, EU and non-EU identical. Fast Track (24 months): €25,630 upfront, or €27,138 in 2 yearly, €28,644 in 4 semester, €30,164 in 24 monthly instalments. Standard (36 months): €31,910 upfront, or €33,794 in 3 yearly, €35,678 in 6 semester, €37,580 in 36 monthly instalments.
tuitionTotal: €25,630 (24-month Fast Track, upfront) to €37,580 (36-month Standard, monthly instalments), 2026/2027 fees. The gap between cheapest and most expensive route is €11,950 for the same qualification.
otherFees: €500 registration fee, included in all quoted prices. No other fees published — UNVERIFIED.
equipmentRequired: PC or Mac laptop recommended, not mandatory. Campus labs supply high-end workstations.
paymentPlans: Four plans on the Standard route and four on Fast Track, all with exact totals published. Paying monthly rather than upfront costs €4,534 extra on Fast Track and €5,670 extra on Standard — a substantial hidden financing charge. No discounts published.
scholarships: None published — UNVERIFIED. DUO student finance explicitly unavailable.
facilities: SAE Amsterdam studios and labs including 3D/immersive audio and mastering facilities.
reputationSignals: The University of Hertfordshire validation is a genuine, verifiable quality anchor and puts this well above SAE's unvalidated diplomas. Fee transparency is excellent. Against it: no Dutch accreditation at all, no visa, the change of awarding body from Middlesex to Hertfordshire in 2022 (institutional churn), and the recurring global SAE complaints about credit transfer and value.
totalCostEstimate: €25,630–€37,580 tuition (registration included) plus Amsterdam living costs across 2–3 years. Given Amsterdam housing costs, realistically €60,000–€90,000+ all-in — for a second bachelor's degree.
recommendation: Wrong level and blocked by visa — rule out. He already has a bachelor's; paying €25,000–€37,000 for a second one is not a rational use of the budget, and the Netherlands route is closed to him anyway because SAE cannot sponsor a residence permit. The one genuinely useful data point here is the English requirement: IELTS 6.0 with 5.5 per band. That tells him what a realistic private-school English bar looks like, versus Berklee Valencia's 7.5 — a difference that should shape how much time he budgets for test prep.

durationEcts: 1 year, part-time (September to September). No ECTS.

deadline: UNVERIFIED — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
tuitionPerYear: Three published tiers, VAT-exempt (CRKBO): FLEX €2,695 | CLASSIC PRAKTIJK €5,975 | ELITE PRAKTIJK €14,475. Same price regardless of nationality — no EU/non-EU distinction.
tuitionTotal: As above — the programme is one year, so the tier price is the total. FLEX €2,695 (online classes, masterclass video library covering 4 years of content, coaching, career guidance, assessments, diploma; studio practice NOT included). CLASSIC PRAKTIJK €5,975 (all-inclusive: full curriculum, all practical lessons, homework support, evaluations, field trips, potential retakes). ELITE PRAKTIJK €14,475 (Classic plus private one-to-one guidance from a chosen renowned producer or sound engineer; no obligation if the preferred mentor cannot be secured).
otherFees: NO VAT (CRKBO-registered). Private studio practice on the FLEX tier charged separately at approximately €40/hour — this is the hidden cost and can add up fast. Application/registration fee: none published — UNVERIFIED. A Music Business Course is INCLUDED free (covering contracts, promotion, playlist placement, sync deals, admin).
paymentPlans: All three tiers payable in 4 QUARTERLY INSTALMENTS. New students get a one-month consideration period before the first invoice is issued — an unusually fair term. No early-bird, alumni or referral discount published.
scholarships: NONE published. No non-EU or Tunisian-specific award. Not eligible for DUO finance (private provider). The 35–50% student software discounts are the only quantifiable benefit.
totalCostEstimate: €2,695 (FLEX, plus ~€40/hr for any studio time) to €14,475 (ELITE). CLASSIC PRAKTIJK at €5,975 all-in is the sensible tier and is genuinely good value for the content — IF you speak Dutch.
visaEligible: NO. A private CRKBO short-vocational provider with a part-time, partly-online programme. Not an IND recognised sponsor (UNVERIFIED but effectively certain — CRKBO providers are not in the IND study register), and part-time/online study cannot support a Dutch student residence permit in any case.
reputationSignals: POSITIVE: operating since 2004 with a long track record; one of the largest part-time audio programmes in the Netherlands; 20+ working-professional teachers; CRKBO + NRTO quality marks; transparent tiered pricing with quarterly instalments and a one-month cooling-off period; free bundled music-business course; real software discounts. RED FLAGS: the FLEX tier at €2,695 delivers online classes with NO included studio time while still awarding the same 'diploma' — the marketing does not foreground this; the €14,475 ELITE tier is a very large sum for a non-accredited private diploma whose main added value is mentor access that is not guaranteed in advance. No published complaints found.
recommendation: NOT VIABLE FOR HIM — DUTCH-LANGUAGE ONLY. This is one of the better-run private audio schools in the Netherlands and the CLASSIC tier at €5,975 all-in is honest value for a Dutch-speaking domestic student. But it is taught in Dutch, it is part-time and partly online, it awards no accredited qualification, and it cannot sponsor a residence permit. Three independent blockers. Reported for completeness of the Dutch private market picture; do not apply.

It describes the programmes as 'internationally recognised, enabling direct entry into the labour market as well as progression to further studies' — 'progression to further studies' is the operative phrase: a BTEC Level 5 is a stepping stone toward a bachelor's, not a postgraduate award. For someone who already holds a BSc, this is a step DOWN in level.

Portuguese study visas generally require enrolment at a recognised education establishment; a DGERT-certified vocational provider outside the higher-education system is a weaker case than a university. Discounts published: Early Bird (reduced base annual tuition for first-time registrants who register in advance, amount UNVERIFIED); alumni/final-year 'special conditions' (amount UNVERIFIED, applied for the whole programme duration).
scholarships: MERIT SCHOLARSHIP (Bolsa de Mérito): students with a final bachelor's average of 15.5 or above — or 16.5 or above for students from FOREIGN institutions — receive a 40% reduction on the base tuition fee, renewed annually provided the average is maintained. This is directly usable by him IF his SMU MedTech GPA converts to 16.5+/20 on the Portuguese scale, which is a high bar (roughly a strong first-class equivalent). Applied to this programme, 40% off would bring tuition to about €3,361/year, €6,723 total. IADE's fees page also mentions a 'Merit Students Programme' with reductions up to 50% for averages of 16+, and 'Bolsa Interna' and 'Bolsa de Apoio ao Estudo' categories — the published table's 10% column corresponds to one of these, subject to limited places. Portuguese State DGES social scholarships are listed but are not realistically open to a new non-EU arrival. A 10% discount for international candidates (limited places, first-come order) is referenced in IADE marketing — UNVERIFIED against the official price list.
intakes: Rolling — 'candidatos podem formalizar candidatura ao longo de todo o ano' (applications accepted year-round), subject to available places. Main start is September.
applicationOpens: Open year-round. No fixed opening date.
deadline: No published fixed deadline — applications accepted throughout the year subject to vacancies. For a September 2027 start with a Tunisian visa file, he should still apply by roughly March–April 2027.
facilities: Sound and image studio ('estúdio de som e imagem'), specialised laboratories and studios. No console, monitoring, Atmos or microphone inventory is published for the sound facilities specifically — UNVERIFIED, and notably thinner disclosure than UCP Porto or Lusófona.
visaEligible: YES. Universidade Europeia/IADE is a State-recognised private university awarding an A3ES-accredited 2-year degree, which supports a D4 study residence visa. As an international-chain university it has established international admissions machinery.
reputationSignals: Positive: A3ES accredited with a specific registration reference; IADE is a long-established and well-regarded Lisbon design school; transparent published price list (better fee disclosure than most schools in this search); a clear, quantified merit scholarship. Negative for HIS purposes: this is a communication/multimedia degree with essentially no sound curriculum — the audio content is one studio and a career-outcomes bullet. Also note the commercial signals: rolling year-round admissions, a discount architecture with at least four overlapping scholarship categories, and mandatory direct debit to access instalments or scholarships. That is a sales-led model, not a selective one.
totalCostEstimate: First-year outlay approx. €6,482 (tuition €5,602.30 + emolumentos €880), before laptop/software and Lisbon living costs. Two-year total tuition + fees approx. €12,085 at base rate; approx. €7,600 if he secures the 40% merit scholarship.
recommendation: DO NOT PRIORITISE — WRONG SUBJECT. The accreditation is genuine, the fees are transparent and the merit scholarship is real and quantified, so it is not a bad institution. But he wants music production, mixing, sound design and electronic music, and this degree teaches digital journalism, infographics, transmedia and web labs. Paying €11,200 for a communication master that touches sound once, in a language he does not speak, would be a poor use of a budget-sensitive candidate's money. Include it only as a distant fallback if UCP, Lusófona and ReSound all fail AND he decides he wants a Portuguese accredited degree for immigration reasons more than he wants sound training. If he does pursue it, the 40% merit scholarship at 16.5+/20 is the only thing that makes the price sensible.

program: Curso Master Producer (Producer I + Producer II) — SHORT COURSE, NOT A MASTER'S DEGREE DESPITE THE NAME
institution: ProDJ Academy
qualification: NOT A DEGREE AND NOT A MASTER'S. The word 'Master' in 'Master Producer' is a marketing label for an advanced course, NOT an academic master's degree. It is a DGERT-certified vocational diploma with no ECTS and no academic grau. This is exactly the naming trap to watch for.
institutionType: Specialist private DJ and electronic-music-production academy (DGERT-certified training entity, not higher education). Describes itself as the only DGERT-certified DJ and music production academy in Portugal.
focus: Electronic music production and DJing in Ableton Live — by far the closest institutional match in Portugal to his stated goal of becoming an international DJ/producer.
whatYouStudy: Producer I: DAW introduction, MIDI manipulation, beat construction, musical composition (scales, chords, progressions), analogue and digital synthesis, audio engineering fundamentals (compression, EQ, mixing), introduction to mastering. Producer II: advanced production processes, mixing techniques, sound design, vocal treatment, compression variations, sidechain effects, professional mastering. Plus 40 hours of professional studio access bookable online and usable up to 3 months after the course ends, 20 hours of 'LAB' Q&A sessions with instructors, four video tutorials with instructor corrections, and access to online classes from other timetables.
durationEcts: 200 hours over approximately 10 months. No ECTS. Multiple weekly timetable options in both cities.
language: Portuguese — UNVERIFIED whether any English-medium delivery exists.
entryRequirements: Extraordinarily low: minimum age 14; basic computer literacy; any special health conditions to be documented at registration. No portfolio, no interview, no prior music knowledge.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — completely. Minimum age 14 and basic computer skills are the only stated requirements. There is no academic prerequisite at all. Be clear-eyed about what that means: this is an open-enrolment commercial course, and the absence of any selection is itself information about what the certificate is worth.
englishTest: None.
tuitionPerYear: €2,490 upfront for the full 200-hour Master Producer course (Lisbon and Porto, same price). Alternatives: 4 monthly instalments of €622.50, or from €320/month over 10 months.
tuitionTotal: €2,490 total tuition (upfront price). The 10-month plan 'from €320/month' implies up to €3,200 if taken over ten payments — a materially higher total, so the instalment route costs more. No non-EU differential published.
otherFees: Enrolment/registration fee €420 (stated to vary by payment method). Diploma issuance fee €45 — charged SEPARATELY, i.e. the certificate itself is an extra. Total realistic outlay: €2,955 upfront (€2,490 + €420 + €45) or up to roughly €3,665 on the 10-month plan. No insurance or materials fee published — UNVERIFIED.
equipmentRequired: Not published as mandatory — UNVERIFIED. In practice an Ableton Live licence and a laptop are needed; the course includes 40 hours of studio access, which partly offsets this. Confirm whether an Ableton licence is included or must be purchased.
paymentPlans: Three published options: upfront €2,490; 4 × €622.50; from €320/month over 10 months. No early-bird, alumni or referral discount published — UNVERIFIED.
scholarships: NONE published — UNVERIFIED.
intakes: MULTIPLE intakes per year — several 2026-2027 start dates published for Lisbon (weekend and weekday options) with more limited availability in Porto. This rolling-intake pattern is typical of commercial academies.
applicationOpens: Rolling — enrol at any time for the next available cohort.
deadline: No deadline; rolling enrolment by cohort start date.
facilities: In-studio learning with professional equipment in both Lisbon and Porto; 40 hours of bookable professional studio time included, usable up to 3 months post-course; 20 hours of LAB mentoring. Detailed equipment inventory not published — UNVERIFIED.
visaEligible: NO. Although the 10-month duration is longer than most courses in this slice, it is still under the 12-month threshold for a D4 study residence visa, and vocational OFP training at a non-higher-education academy is not a recognised visa-sponsoring category. ProDJ publishes nothing about visa support for non-EU students. He CANNOT move to Portugal on this.
reputationSignals: Positive and genuinely relevant: DGERT certification (it claims to be the only DGERT-certified DJ/production academy in Portugal), instructors holding CCP pedagogical credentials, two campuses, included studio hours, and a syllabus squarely aimed at electronic music and DJing — which is what he actually wants. Negative: age-14 minimum and no selection whatsoever; the 'Master Producer' name invites exactly the confusion this report exists to prevent; a separate €45 charge to issue the diploma; an enrolment fee (€420–€520) that varies by payment method, which is an odd and slightly opaque practice; and instalment plans that increase the total cost without this being flagged. No independent graduate-outcome data or notable alumni published.
totalCostEstimate: €2,955 all-in paying upfront (tuition €2,490 + enrolment €420 + diploma €45). Up to roughly €3,665 on the 10-month instalment plan. Plus living costs if attending in person in Lisbon or Porto (~€900–€1,300/month for 10 months = €9,000–€13,000) — which dwarfs the tuition and is unfunded and visa-less.
recommendation: CLOSEST TO WHAT HE WANTS TO DO, FURTHEST FROM WHAT HE NEEDS INSTITUTIONALLY. Be direct with him: if the only goal were 'learn to produce electronic music and DJ', this is the most on-target training in Portugal, and €2,955 is not unreasonable for 200 hours plus 40 studio hours. But it is not a master's despite its name, it confers no academic credit, and critically it CANNOT get him a residence permit — so he would be paying €12,000+ including living costs to sit in Lisbon on a tourist footing with no legal study status. The rational play is the inverse: use an accredited master's (UCP Porto, Lusófona, or funded ReSound) to obtain the visa and the residence permit, and then, once legally resident, add a ProDJ or ETIC specialisation as a cheap evening top-up. Never the other way round.

program: ReSound — Erasmus Mundus Joint Master of Arts in Sound Design for Media Arts
institution: Consortium: IADT Dún Laoghaire (Ireland) + Universidade Lusófona (Portugal, PRIVATE) + Lithuanian Academy of Music and Theatre (Lithuania), within the FilmEU European University alliance
city: Lisbon (semester 2; semester 1 Dublin, semester 3 Vilnius, semester 4 at any partner)
country: Portugal (one of three countries; the Portuguese partner is the private Universidade Lusófona)
qualification: ERASMUS MUNDUS JOINT MASTER (EMJM) — 120 ECTS joint/multiple master's degree awarded by the consortium partners. A full, official 2nd-cycle degree, not a certificate.
institutionType: International consortium; the Portuguese leg is a private university (Universidade Lusófona / COFAC). IADT is an Irish public institute; LMTA is a Lithuanian public academy.
accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL and the highest-quality signal available in this slice. Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are selected and funded directly by the European Commission (project 101180273) and each partner's award is nationally accredited — Lusófona's contribution sits under A3ES, IADT under QQI/Ireland, LMTA under Lithuanian accreditation. EMJM designation is itself an external quality endorsement.
focus: Sound as an artistic, cultural and technological force across media arts, immersive environments, performance and the audiovisual industries — the most internationally-facing sound master's touching Portugal.
whatYouStudy: Four semesters with structured mobility: Semester 1 at IADT (Ireland); Semester 2 at Universidade Lusófona (Lisbon); Semester 3 at LMTA (Vilnius); Semester 4 master's thesis/project at any partner. Detailed per-semester module lists were not extractable from the pages read — UNVERIFIED; request the full programme handbook from the consortium. The Lisbon semester draws on Lusófona's Atmos/3D audio, multitrack studios and acoustic labs.
durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS, full-time, in-person, with compulsory mobility across three countries.
language: English — this is the decisive difference from every other accredited option in Portugal.
entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree in sound, music, film, or media studies. Critically, the published wording states: 'Applicants with degrees in other fields may also be considered if they possess relevant prior experience' in areas such as sound, music, film or media. Application pack: academic transcripts, portfolio, TWO recommendation letters, proof of English proficiency. Maximum 24 places per year.
acceptsNonMusic: CONDITIONALLY YES, and this is the exact clause he must clear. Quote: 'Applicants with degrees in other fields may also be considered if they possess relevant prior experience.' A Software Engineering BSc is a 'degree in another field', so admission turns entirely on evidencing 'relevant prior experience' in sound/music/film/media. He currently has NONE — no music degree, no conservatory training, no professional audio work. Between now and a January-2027 deadline he must manufacture that evidence: released tracks, credited sound work on short films or games, live sets, an audio software project. Without it, this is a rejection.
portfolioSpec: Exactly specified, unusually clearly: maximum 3 examples of sound or media-related work; a single hyperlink to a portfolio site or a compiled file is acceptable; each piece needs a short reflective paragraph stating his role; total realistic listening/viewing time 10–15 minutes. Note the discipline this demands — three strong pieces, not a dump.
auditionSpec: No audition or performance test published. Selection is on documents, portfolio and references; an interview stage is UNVERIFIED.
englishTest: YES — and this is his action item. IELTS 6.0 minimum with ALL components at 6.0 or above. Equivalents accepted: TOEFL iBT 79, Duolingo 110, Cambridge B2, LanguageCert ESOL. Tests must be within 2 years of application. Alternative: completion of an EQF Level 4+ qualification with at least one year taught in English — worth checking whether his SMU MedTech BSc, if English-taught, qualifies him for this waiver, as that would save both the fee and the sitting. He has NOT taken IELTS; on a January 2027 deadline he must book it by roughly October 2027... i.e. autumn 2026, immediately.
tuitionPerYear: €7,500 per year for self-funded students (participation costs), charged as €7,500 at semester 1 and €7,500 at semester 3, per the official consortium site. Non-EU pricing is stated to be IDENTICAL to EU pricing — no partner-country surcharge, which is unusual and favourable.
tuitionTotal: €15,000 total for the four-semester programme (self-funded). CONFLICT FLAG: Universidade Lusófona's own ReSound page instead quotes an average of about €2,250 per month for 30-ECTS semestral units (roughly €9,000 per semester), which does not reconcile with the consortium's €15,000 total. Treat the consortium figure (resound-ma.eu) as authoritative and get the discrepancy resolved in writing before applying.
otherFees: No application fee is mentioned on the application page. Travel, accommodation and living costs are explicitly excluded and estimated by the consortium at €600–€1,000 per month. Because of the three-country mobility, he should also budget for THREE residence-permit processes (Ireland, Portugal, Lithuania) and inter-country relocation — a real, unpublished cost that could easily add €1,500–€3,000 across the two years. UNVERIFIED as a published figure.
equipmentRequired: Not published — UNVERIFIED. A capable laptop and headphones are a practical necessity for a mobility-based sound programme.
paymentPlans: Self-funded tuition is split into two payments (€7,500 at semester 1, €7,500 at semester 3) rather than four. No instalment, early-bird or alumni discount published — UNVERIFIED.
scholarships: THE BEST SCHOLARSHIP AVAILABLE ANYWHERE IN THIS SEARCH, and it is open to him as a non-EU national. Erasmus Mundus scholarships cover FULL tuition (he pays €0) plus a stipend of €1,400 PER MONTH, which is explicitly described as contributing to travel, visa and living allowance. Over 24 months that is roughly €33,600 in stipend plus €15,000 in waived tuition — around €48,600 of value. Awarded on merit. Number of scholarships is a limited share of the maximum 24 annual places — so it is genuinely competitive, but EMJM calls typically reserve a substantial quota for Partner Country (non-EU) applicants, which is his category. This is the single item in this whole Portuguese slice that could make his plan free instead of self-funded.
intakes: One intake per year, September.
applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. The 2026 intake round opened in autumn 2025. Expect the round for a September 2027 start to open around October–November 2026 — i.e. within months of now. He should be monitoring resound-ma.eu from October 2026.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. The last published deadline was extended to 27 January 2026 for the 2026 entry; applications for 2026 are now closed. Expect a comparable late-January 2027 deadline for September 2027 entry. Erasmus Mundus scholarship deadlines are hard and are NOT extended for late portfolios.
facilities: Lisbon semester: Lusófona's professional multitrack studios, acoustic laboratories, cinema post-production and 3D Atmos room. Dublin: IADT's media production facilities. Vilnius: LMTA. Plus the FilmEU alliance network of artists, producers and researchers across Europe.
visaEligible: YES, and better than a single-country route in one respect: Erasmus Mundus students receive structured institutional support for visas at each partner, and the €1,400/month stipend comfortably satisfies proof-of-means tests. Counterpoint: three separate immigration processes in two years is administratively heavy for a Tunisian passport holder, and Ireland is outside Schengen — factor in Irish immigration (IRP) separately from the Schengen leg.
reputationSignals: European Commission selection and funding; FilmEU European University alliance membership; three national accreditations; capped at 24 students a year (so genuinely small cohorts); explicit English-medium delivery. This is the most prestigious sound qualification reachable through a private Portuguese institution. No red flags found. The only structural caveat is that only ONE of four semesters is actually in Portugal, so if his goal is to establish himself in Lisbon specifically, this scatters him across three countries.
totalCostEstimate: With an Erasmus Mundus scholarship: effectively €0 tuition and a net-positive €1,400/month. Without a scholarship: €15,000 tuition + roughly €14,400–€24,000 living over 24 months + relocation/permits, i.e. a realistic all-in €31,000–€42,000 over two years.
recommendation: APPLY. THIS IS HIS SINGLE HIGHEST-VALUE SHOT IN THE PORTUGUESE SLICE — and the only one that is taught in English and can be fully funded. The maths is decisive: an Erasmus Mundus scholarship converts a €30k+ plan into a funded one with a €1,400/month stipend, which for a budget-sensitive Tunisian self-payer is transformative. But be blunt with him about the odds and the work: 24 places, worldwide competition, and an admission clause that requires 'relevant prior experience' he does not yet have. His concrete twelve-month plan should be (1) book IELTS now and clear 6.0 in every band — or verify his BSc's English-medium waiver; (2) build the three portfolio pieces the spec asks for, at 10–15 minutes total, ideally one released track, one piece of sound-to-picture, and one audio-software/interactive piece that leverages his engineering background as a differentiator rather than a liability; (3) secure two recommenders now; (4) watch for the call opening around October 2026. If he only does one thing from this entire Portugal report, it should be this application — with UCP Porto and Lusófona's own mestrado as the paid fallbacks.

Absent any of those, it is the school's own diploma — a título propio in substance. Note that CEV DOES deliver an officially regulated 'Técnico Superior en Sonido para Audiovisuales y Espectáculos' (a Grado Superior vocational qualification), which is official but is a VOCATIONAL, sub-degree award, not a master. Do not let the presence of official vocational programmes at the school imply that this master is official.
visaEligible: UNVERIFIED. Nothing about non-EU student visas is published for this programme. A 1,200-hour, one-year, in-person programme is at least structurally full-time, which helps, but confirmation must be obtained in writing.

durationEcts: 1 year, 1,200 hours. No ECTS published.
intakes: One intake per year, in October.

This is the most conventionally musical of the Madrid private masters.
auditionSpec: None published, though the instrumental module suggests some level check is likely.
englishTest: No IELTS required. Taught in Spanish.
deadline: No published deadline. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for October 2027.
tuitionPerYear: €7,245 for the programme, per the educaweb listing for the Madrid campus. CEV's own site lists the price as 'consultar con el centro' — so this figure is aggregator-sourced and should be confirmed directly. Academic year of the figure is UNVERIFIED.
tuitionTotal: €7,245 total for the one-year programme (aggregator-sourced; confirm with CEV). No separate non-EU rate is published.
otherFees: UNVERIFIED — no application, matriculation, materials or exam fees are published.
equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED. The syllabus covers DAWs, sound-design software, synthesis and sampling, so a laptop and DAW licence should be assumed.
totalCostEstimate: Approximately €7,245 tuition plus Madrid living costs, plus unpublished fees and equipment — realistically €19,000–€23,000 for a first year including living expenses, but the tuition figure itself needs direct confirmation.
paymentPlans: UNVERIFIED — none published.
scholarships: UNVERIFIED — none published. Nothing is advertised for non-EU applicants.

Teaching staff are described as active industry professionals with company links that bring real case studies into the classroom.
reputationSignals: CEV holds a CUM LAUDE seal (2019) with an average student rating of 4.6/5, with reviews praising the teaching staff and modern facilities. program: Máster en Producción Musical Discográfica e Ingeniería de Sonido (MPD)
institution: CICE — La Escuela Profesional de Nuevas Tecnologías
institutionType: Private technology/creative-industries training school and authorised certification centre
qualification: A CICE school 'Máster' — a private professional certificate, bundled with vendor certifications (Avid Pro Tools, Waves Level A). No university validation and no ECTS are published.
accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL. The word 'Oficial' in the programme title refers to OFFICIAL AVID CERTIFICATION — a software-vendor credential — NOT to Spanish academic accreditation. This is an important and easily-missed marketing construction: 'Máster ... - Oficial de AVID' means Avid-official, not ANECA-official. There is no ANECA verification, no validating university, no ECTS, no EHEA status and no PhD access. It is a private certificate.
visaEligible: UNVERIFIED / DOUBTFUL. Nothing about non-EU student visas is published. CICE also offers this master ONLINE, which would not support a residence permit at all. Do not assume visa eligibility.
focus: Record production and sound engineering: sound capture, audio processors, mixing, mastering, genre-specific mixing approaches, and vendor certification.
whatYouStudy: A 10-module programme covering foundational and advanced topics: capture of acoustic and electronic sound sources, audio processors, mixing techniques, mastering, and genre-specific mixing approaches. Includes preparation for Official Waves Level A Certification.
durationEcts: UNVERIFIED. No duration in months or hours and no ECTS is published on the sources read.
language: Spanish, with 'elementary English competency' listed as an entry requirement.
intakes: UNVERIFIED. Available in-person in Madrid and also online.

englishTest: No IELTS. 'Elementary English competency' is stated as a requirement; instruction is in Spanish.
deadline: UNVERIFIED — no published deadline. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.

Another reference gives €5,100 for the master including Waves Level A certification but explicitly NOT including the Pro Tools certifications. A general indication is that CICE masters run around €4,500 and courses around €2,000. CICE's own site was not reachable to confirm. Treat all of these as UNVERIFIED.
tuitionTotal: UNVERIFIED — no current, officially published figure exists in the sources read.
otherFees: IMPORTANT: at least one source states the €5,100 price includes Waves Level A certification but does NOT include the Avid Pro Tools certifications — meaning the vendor exams that are the programme's main selling point may be billed separately. Exam-fee amounts UNVERIFIED. Application, enrolment and materials fees UNVERIFIED.
equipmentRequired: Mac OS proficiency is an entry requirement, which strongly implies a Mac is expected. Pro Tools familiarity is expected on entry, implying a licence. Neither cost is published.

scholarships: UNVERIFIED — none published; nothing for non-EU applicants.

For a software engineer who wants Pro Tools and Waves credentials quickly and cheaply it has real utility — but it is not a postgraduate qualification, it will not support a visa, and it points at studio engineering rather than DJing or electronic production. program: Máster en Producción Musical Profesional

institutionType: Specialist audio/DJ academy — independent private school partnered with a private university

UDIMA's own page for the associated Máster Profesional en Producción Musical states in terms: 'enseñanza no reglada y sin carácter oficial' — non-regulated teaching with no official character. No ANECA verification, no EHEA official master status, no PhD access.
visaEligible: UNLIKELY AS STRUCTURED / UNVERIFIED. The programme runs 9 months in EVENING sessions only, Monday to Thursday 19:00–21:30 — that is a part-time evening schedule, which is a poor basis for a Spanish full-time student visa. DJP's page notes only that international students without a Spanish bank account should contact admissions about payment methods; it makes no visa claim. He must not assume this programme can host a residence permit.
focus: Electronic and contemporary music production, DAW-centred, with live performance and music marketing — genuinely close to the DJ/producer target.
whatYouStudy: Seven modules: (1) DAW Production; (2) Applied Musical Fundamentals; (3) Composition and Songwriting; (4) Synthesis and Sound Design; (5) Live Performance; (6) Mixing and Mastering; (7) Marketing and Music Promotion. Taught on Ableton Live, Logic Pro, FL Studio and Reaper. Includes masterclasses with working producers.
durationEcts: 9 months; 60 ECTS (as issued by UDIMA).

entryRequirements: Not explicitly published on the programme page. The linked UDIMA description says the programme targets anyone 'interested in developing music production skills, whether from scratch or from an intermediate level', including musicians, composers, producers, sound engineers and DJs — no formal prerequisites are stated.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — effectively open access. UDIMA's description explicitly welcomes beginners ('ya sea desde cero') and no music degree or prior experience is required. His profile is unambiguously accepted. That accessibility is also the warning sign: an award that anyone can enter carries correspondingly little selection signal.
englishTest: None required. Taught in Spanish — Spanish is the real language barrier here, not English.
applicationOpens: Rolling until places fill for the September start.
deadline: No published deadline; enrolment runs up to the September start. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for September 2027.
tuitionPerYear: €1,200 enrolment + €4,700 tuition = €5,900 total in a single payment; or €1,200 enrolment + 10 monthly payments of €490 = €6,100 total on the instalment plan. (Figures as published for the 21 September 2026 cohort.)
tuitionTotal: €5,900 (single payment) or €6,100 (instalments) for the whole 9-month programme. No separate non-EU rate is published — non-EU students pay the same.
otherFees: The €1,200 'matrícula' (enrolment) is charged on top of tuition and is included in both totals above. No other application, materials or exam fees are published. Whether the €1,200 is refundable is UNVERIFIED.
equipmentRequired: A laptop and a DAW are implied by the syllabus. The school partly offsets this: students receive 50% off Ableton Live Suite and 30–50% off plugins — a real, quantified saving that most competitors do not publish.
totalCostEstimate: €5,900–€6,100 in tuition and enrolment, plus a laptop and DAW licence (Ableton Live Suite at the 50% student rate), plus Madrid living costs. Total first-year outlay realistically €18,000–€22,000 including living expenses. This is one of the cheapest master-branded options in the slice.
paymentPlans: Two published options: single payment (€1,200 + €4,700) or 10 monthly instalments of €490 after the €1,200 enrolment. No interest is mentioned. No early-bird, alumni or referral discount is published. International students without a Spanish bank account are told to contact admissions for alternative payment arrangements — arrange this before committing.
scholarships: None published. No bursary, fee waiver or non-EU award is advertised.
facilities: In-person only at Calle Pilar de Zaragoza 63, Madrid. Access to Ableton Live, Logic Pro, FL Studio and Reaper; a virtual learning platform; exclusive masterclasses with professional producers; and substantial software discounts (50% Ableton Live Suite, 30–50% plugins).
reputationSignals: DJP is an established Madrid DJ/production school that has also launched an internationally-validated HND in music production, which suggests some quality-assurance discipline. The UDIMA partnership gives a paper trail. RED FLAGS: UDIMA itself labels the associated programme 'sin carácter oficial'; the evening-only schedule undermines any visa story; and the ECTS-to-contact-hours ratio (60 ECTS from Mon–Thu 19:00–21:30 over 9 months) looks generous relative to actual teaching time.
recommendation: Cheap, DJ/producer-relevant, and open to exactly his profile — on content-per-euro it is arguably the best value in this slice. But I would not build an immigration plan on it: the evening-only schedule makes it a weak student-visa vehicle, and the qualification is explicitly non-official. My candid verdict: excellent as a skills purchase if he is already legally in Spain, poor as a route INTO Spain. If he wants both craft and residency he should choose a full-time programme instead. Ask admissions, in writing, one question: 'Does enrolment on this programme support a Spanish student visa for a Tunisian national?' — and act on the answer.

program: COVERAGE CHECK — Máster Superior de Especialidad: Sonido (existence indicated, details unpublished)

program: Master of Science in Acoustics, Audio and Vibrations (Máster Universitario en Acústica, Audio y Vibraciones)

otherFees: UNVERIFIED. Academic Excellence Scholarship: 50% (GPA 9.5+), 40% (GPA 8.5+), 20% (GPA 8.0+) — 2 to 4 awards per programme; open to international students if the GPA system is comparable. La Salle Boost Scholarships: 10–40% for strong academic/professional record or limited financial resources; 25% for disability ≥33%. Lasallians Scholarship 10% for alumni of any La Salle school worldwide. Partner University Scholarship 15%. 'la Caixa' Foundation international master's grants (70% of registration fee) are also referenced. NOT available to him: Massó Foundation (Spanish/EU/legal residents only), Casa de México (Mexican nationals), Carolina Foundation (Ibero-American), #SheTechs (women; and non-EU candidates need a work permit). CRITICAL RULE published by La Salle: 'Different scholarships, discounts, and financial aid options cannot be combined.'
paymentPlans: Not published on the programme page — UNVERIFIED. FUNDAE company-subsidised training is referenced but applies to employees of Spanish companies, not to him.

reputationSignals: Universitat Ramon Llull is one of Spain's most established private universities; La Salle has a long track record in audio/acoustics engineering and also runs an official Master in Architectural and Environmental Acoustics and an MSc in Digital Arts and Creative Technologies. Taught in English with a 30-student cap. No red flags found.
recommendation: The strongest DEGREE in this slice for him, and the weakest fit for his stated goal. It is an official Spanish master, taught in English, at a serious private university, aimed squarely at engineering graduates — it is the one programme here where his BSc in Software Engineering is an advantage rather than a liability, and where no portfolio and no musicianship proof is needed. It also has real published scholarships (up to 50% on GPA alone) and a clean visa path. But it will NOT make him a DJ or a music producer: it is noise control, vibrations and signal processing for automotive/aerospace/construction. Recommend it only if his priority shifts to 'get to Europe with a real, fundable, visa-safe technical degree and build the music career on the side in Barcelona' — which, given his profile and budget sensitivity, is a genuinely defensible strategy. First action: email admissions to confirm (a) Software Engineering counts as a 'similar' degree, (b) the tuition figure, (c) the IELTS band.

recommendation: The best CRAFT fit in Spain for his stated goal — this is literally an electronic-music-production master taught on Ableton and hardware synths, with no music degree required and his software-engineering BSc accepted outright. Second, the price is not published anywhere, which for a budget-sensitive self-payer is a serious governance problem — get it in writing before engaging. My verdict: pursue it as a strong second option behind Berklee, but treat the unpublished fee and the visa question as blockers to clear in writing first.
